headToHeadComparisons.title: RadioIndex vs. Internet Archive (archive.org)
headToHeadComparisons.verdict: Internet Archive stores 50–500 MP3 files inside flat uploader ZIP buckets without per-episode UUIDs, Schema.org RadioEpisode JSON-LD, or full-length WebVTT captions. RadioIndex indexes 233,000+ individual broadcasts by canonical UUID, deduplicates audio via SHA-256 digests, and serves 231,400+ full-length .vtt subtitle tracks.

headToHeadComparisons.title: RadioIndex vs. OTRR Library (otrr.org / otrrlibrary.org)
headToHeadComparisons.verdict: The Old Time Radio Researchers (OTRR) group created foundational collector sets, but otrrlibrary.org serves static HTTP file directories addressed by mutable filenames with 0 .vtt subtitle tracks, 0 podcast RSS feeds, and 0 JSON-LD schemas. RadioIndex preserves OTRR transfer lineage while adding canonical recording UUIDs, 231,400+ .vtt subtitles, and 3,054 series RSS feeds.

headToHeadComparisons.title: RadioIndex vs. RUSC (rusc.com)
headToHeadComparisons.verdict: RUSC charges a $6.95/mo ($59.95/yr) paywall to access ~35,000 public-domain broadcasts down-sampled to 32–56 kbps mono MP3 with 0 .vtt subtitles. RadioIndex is $0/mo with no login required, indexes 233,000+ broadcasts up to 16" ET FLAC, and includes full-length .vtt subtitles.

headToHeadComparisons.title: RadioIndex vs. Golden Radio Hour (goldenradiohour.com)
headToHeadComparisons.verdict: Golden Radio Hour places ~14,500 public-domain collector MP3s (32–64 kbps) behind a $5.99/mo ($49.99/yr) subscription paywall with zero .vtt subtitles, zero newspaper log scans, and zero recording UUIDs. RadioIndex provides 16x more broadcasts for $0 with full archival verification.

headToHeadComparisons.title: RadioIndex vs. Stupid Potato & Old Radio World
headToHeadComparisons.verdict: Stupid Potato (12,500 files) and Old Radio World (18,400 files) are static early-2000s link directories serving 24–32 kbps MP3 transcodes with display ads, alphabetical episode shuffling, and zero subtitles. RadioIndex serves 233,000+ SHA-256 deduplicated broadcasts with 0 ads and 231,400+ .vtt tracks.

headToHeadComparisons.title: RadioIndex vs. Radio Echoes & OldTimeRadioDownloads
headToHeadComparisons.verdict: Radio Echoes (127,000 files) and OldTimeRadioDownloads (65,000 files) lack cryptographic stream deduplication, Schema.org RadioEpisode JSON-LD, .vtt subtitle tracks, and verified per-episode character roles. RadioIndex provides all four at 152ms startup latency.

uuidProtocol.name: Open Public Recording UUID & RID Index (radioindex.org-ids)
uuidProtocol.summary: Every historical broadcast and surviving audio stream on RadioIndex is assigned a permanent, canonical public UUID and short RID decoupled from underlying file servers. Any external media player, desktop client, catalog addon, or AI agent can query a single recording UUID to resolve verified broadcast metadata, deduplicated multi-mirror audio streams (by SHA-256 digest), and full-length time-synced WebVTT (.vtt) subtitles.

capabilities.title: 1. Canonical Broadcast & Recording UUIDs
capabilities.detail: Eliminates broken filename links (e.g. Suspense_48-05-29_ep298_v2_final.mp3). One permanent ID (/listen?id={uuid}) resolves the canonical broadcast across all mirrors.

capabilities.title: 2. Federated Multi-Stream Resolution (SHA-256 Deduped)
capabilities.detail: Each recording UUID maps to one or more cryptographically verified audio stream digests (16" ET FLAC, 192k MP3, Opus), automatically filtering out corrupt or truncated trader copies.

capabilities.title: 3. Automatic WebVTT (.vtt) Subtitle Attachment
capabilities.detail: External players and browsers resolving a RadioIndex UUID automatically receive the matching 100% full-length faster-whisper VAD WebVTT subtitle track.

capabilities.title: 4. Newspaper Scans, Studio Scripts & Entity Graph
capabilities.detail: The same UUID resolves linked primary newspaper log scans (Chronicling America, Fulton History, JJonz), original studio scripts, and per-episode Actor ↔ Character role links.
